text: Parametric equations give both coordinates in terms of a shared parameter. Let the horizontal coordinate equal t and the vertical coordinate equal t squared. As t varies, these paired outputs trace the familiar parabola while retaining an order of travel.
title: Idea 1

text: Evaluate both rules at the same parameter value. Negative two gives negative two, four; zero gives the origin; and positive two gives two, four. Mixing coordinates from different parameter values would create a point that the motion never actually visits at that time.
title: Idea 2

text: A different pair of rules traces a circle. Cosine and sine automatically satisfy x squared plus y squared equals one. As the parameter increases from zero to two pi, the point travels counterclockwise through one complete turn.
title: Idea 3

text: Doubling the parameter inside both functions traces the same geometric circle twice as quickly. Eliminating the parameter reveals the circle equation but loses this timing information. A curve can therefore have many parametrizations with different directions, speeds, or numbers of traversals.
title: Idea 4
